Samir — thanks for the clear asks. We're aligned on the principle (limited temporary activation for availability/reliability incidents) and can propose specific language that preserves our operational agility while meeting BrightHealth's documentation needs.

High-level proposal (for inclusion in the US state addendum / service-provider section):

- Emergency Subprocessor Activation. Notwithstanding any notice requirements in this Addendum, Redwood may temporarily engage a subprocessor to address an emergency affecting service availability ("Emergency Subprocessor") for a maximum initial duration of 72 hours. Redwood will provide written notification to Customer within 48 hours of activation describing the identity of the Emergency Subprocessor, reason for activation, anticipated duration, and categories of Customer Data accessed.

- Post-Event Attestation & Evidence. Within 10 business days following the end of the activation period, Redwood will provide Customer with: (a) a signed attestation describing the timeline of activation and deactivation; (b) a data processing scope summary (categories of data and processing operations performed); (c) confirmation of region(s) where processing occurred; and (d) confirmation that no Customer Data was retained beyond the activation period, or, if retained, steps to securely delete and a retention justification.

Notes/constraints:
- We cannot provide granular logs that include customer PII in raw form as part of the standard attestation; however, we can provide redacted event summaries and signed process evidence from our infra team.
- For on-prem or air-gapped customers we may require an alternative manual attestation flow.

I've attached a tracked-change draft of the addendum with the proposed clause (CCPA_addendum_emergency-subproc-diff.docx). Please review and flag any Redlines you need. If this looks acceptable, we can route through your legal ops and our privacy team for final sign-off — estimated 3-5 business days for internal review.

Proposed next step: 20-minute call tomorrow to confirm language and evidence format. Are you available at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan

Looping in Aditya and Grace to confirm the operational commitments and evidence we can reliably provide. Quick points so legal has a consistent reply: 

- Timeline & attestation: we can produce a signed timeline (SOC2 ops lead + oncall engineer) within 10 business days. That will include start/end timestamps, region(s), and a categorical list of data types processed.
- Retention confirmation: by default our caches/edge nodes use ephemeral storage; we can confirm no data persisted beyond 24 hours under normal emergency flow. For some connectors (legacy S3 proxy) there may be logs that persist 30 days — we'll provide deletion plans in those cases.
- Evidence packages: create a "redaction-safe" attachment template: a) signed attestation PDF, b) sanitized processing summary CSV, c) infra manifest (service names + regions).
- Exceptions: if a customer insists on raw log exports, we escalate to privacy + legal and require a DPA amendment and PO.

Aditya — can your team commit to the 10 business day attestation SLA and the redaction template? If not, propose the alternate with timelines.
